content.overview: BNS s. 183 — Effacing writing from substance bearing Government stamp, or removing from document a stamp used for it, with intent to cause loss to Government.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Effacing writing from substance bearing Government stamp, or removing from document a stamp used for it, with intent to cause loss to Government. BNS restatement of IPC 261. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 261. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 183 is the rule on “Effacing writing from substance bearing Government stamp, or removing from document a stamp used for it, with intent to cause loss to Government”. The section provides that effacing writing from substance bearing Government stamp, or removing from document a stamp used for it, with intent to cause loss to Government. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 183 exists so that “Effacing writing from substance bearing Government stamp, or removing from document a stamp used for it, with intent to cause loss to Government” has a closed legal test in Chapter X — Of Offences Relating to Coin, Currency-Notes, Bank-Notes and Government Stamps. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Counterfeiting is merged. Currency-note forgeries that lived across IPC 489A–E sit here.

The provision in detail
Effacing writing from substance bearing Government stamp, or removing from document a stamp used for it, with intent to cause loss to Government

183. Whoever, fraudulently or with intent to cause loss to the Government, removes or effaces from any substance, bearing any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, any writing or document for which such stamp has been used, or removes from any writing or document a stamp which has been used for such writing or document, in order that such stamp may be used for a different writing or document, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
